audit_2026_11_04: FRESH AUDIT PASSED (first-hand, 2026-11-04) — Detroit/Wayne was second on the re-audit-first list from the 2026-10-31 corrections: that run's Detroit skips were RETRACTED the same night because BSEED's services flap between snapshots, and a fresh audit with repeated-read stability checks was ordered before any build or skip. This audit ran that discipline. (1) STABILITY: three full audit passes over ~5 minutes (01:59Z, 02:00Z, 02:04Z) returned IDENTICAL figures for both BSEED layers — building: 48,081 rows all-time, every row carrying an issued_date, max issued 2026-11-03, trailing-12-month 6,091, Sep 2026 514 — matching the retraction's verified snapshot (47,980 / 6,039 / 514) within two days of live growth, and NOT either flapped snapshot (the issuance-cliff snapshot or the doubled snapshot). (2) Wayne County's report combines BOTH BSEED registers — building (this registry) and trades (detroit-wayne-mi-trades) — into one county hub, each register pulled and gated separately under its own registry. (3) IDENTITY: one row per permit — window rows 6,091 = 6,091 distinct record_id, 0 null; the two registers' record_id families are disjoint (building RES-/BLD-, trades MEC-/PLM-/ELE-/FAP-/ELV-/BPV-/GTP-), measured overlap 0. (4) COVERAGE: City of Detroit only (BSEED is Detroit's permitting department); Wayne County's other municipalities publish separately and are not in these feeds. BSEED demolition permits are a separate city dataset and are NOT in either register — the exclusion is labeled on the hub (the Raleigh treatment). (5) TERMS: both ArcGIS items are public (owner topsoil.integration_detroitmi, the City of Detroit's open-data integration account — these services feed the city's open-data program); their item records carry no license text and no restriction on reuse; figures are published 'as reported by the City of Detroit' with attribution, no endorsement implied. Audit evidence: ~/workspace/goals/permitsbycounty/hidden_files/expansion-2026-11-04/.
coverage_note: Building permits issued by the City of Detroit (BSEED building register), combined on the county hub with the city's trades register. Detroit only; other Wayne County municipalities publish separately.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one record_id in BSEED's building register. The register's grain is one row per issued permit; no collapsing is needed or applied.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (issued_date >= 2025-11-04), measured 2026-11-04 on repeated stability-checked reads: 6,091 rows = 6,091 distinct record_id, 0 null record_id, 0 missing address. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull. The building and trades registers' record_id families are disjoint (measured overlap 0 in the window).

field_map.address: address, as published (present on 100% of window rows). City is Detroit, the issuing jurisdiction; ZIP is zip_code (missing on 16 of 6,091 window rows).
field_map.application_date: submitted_date (ArcGIS DateOnly). Published on every window row.
field_map.category: No honest category exists: the register's proposed/current use fields are a many-valued building-use vocabulary (OFFICE / Urban Garden / dwellings under several spellings), and its RES- and BLD- record series both carry dwellings — category stays NULL (the Boston treatment).
field_map.contractor_rule: The building register publishes NO contractor or business-name field, so contractor_name stays NULL for building permits, never inferred. (The trades register does publish a business of record — see detroit-wayne-mi-trades.)
field_map.issue_date: issued_date (ArcGIS DateOnly). The window is defined on it: a record enters this report when BSEED records an issue date. Every row in the register carries one.
field_map.permit_number: record_id (BSEED's public permit number, e.g. RES2026-04046).
field_map.permit_type: permit_type, the city's own family naming (Alteration, New, Change of Use, Residential Rehab, ...), read by trades.classify_detroit_trade: New / New Revision / Foundation Only -> new-construction; the remaining building families name no single licensed trade -> general.
field_map.status: The register publishes no status field — it is an issued-permits register, so status is 'issued' by the register's own definition and status_source stays NULL (the Baton Rouge treatment).
field_map.valuation: amt_estimated_contractor_cost — the applicant's estimated cost of the work — PASSED validation on the full window (measured 2026-11-04) and publishes ON BUILDING PERMITS ONLY (the Fort Worth treatment: the trades register publishes no cost field at all, so the county's reported value is the building permits' stated total, disclosed wherever the total appears). Evidence: a figure is stated on 6,090 of 6,091 window permits, 6,062 above $1, only 27 at $0/$1 (0.4% — the Austin placeholder disease absent), median $12,500; the DB sum after load is $2,650,410,876 across the 6,089 permits that carry a stored value. ONE stated figure is negative — RES2025-04784 (an alteration at 4400 Chalmers St) states -$1,693, an applicant sign typo in an otherwise ordinary permit: the first backfill held that record at gate 3 (negative valuation); the mapping was then corrected to exclude the impossible VALUE (carried NULL) while the permit itself counts, the SOP section 5 'exclude bad records' remedy applied to the bad field, and the re-run accepted 6,091 with held 0. Disclosed here and in the normalizer. Shapes disclosed: the largest permit ($874,050,000, a New permit at 2850 W Grand Blvd) appears exactly once and is 33.0% of the total — a single flagship project, the Chicago shape; repeated values above $1M are round applicant budgets (the Boston signature) or same-address revision restatements (e.g. $56,300,000 on two Alter Revision permits at 6051 Hastings St), bounding any restatement excess at a few percent. amt_permit_cost is the city's permit FEE, not a project value — it is never carried as a valuation. Re-validate only if the field changes character.

history_range: issued_date 2019-01-02 onward in the source (48,081 rows); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: Public access via the City of Detroit's ArcGIS organization (open-data integration account); no reuse restriction stated in the item record; attribution: City of Detroit (BSEED)
rate_limit: ArcGIS hosted FeatureServer query, 1,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the audit and backfill pulls steadily. Note (measured 2026-10-31 and honored in this build): these services have served flapping snapshots in the past — audits use repeated passes, and gate 4's count-match plus baseline guards every pull.
source_name: City of Detroit — BSEED Building Permits
terms_status: verified-open-2026-11-04: the ArcGIS item 'Building Permits' (publisher: City of Detroit BSEED via its open-data integration account topsoil.integration_detroitmi; access public) carries no license text of its own and no restriction on reuse; the service feeds the City of Detroit open-data program; figures are published 'as reported by the City of Detroit' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Live register (permits issued 2026-11-03, the day before the audit, are in the feed). Freshness (gate 5) is measured from the layer's own editingInfo.dataLastEditDate under a 96h threshold.
watermark_field: issued_date + record_id — refresh re-pulls by the issued_date watermark and upserts.
